title: GraphQLReactorClient is a light Switchboard-only client that fills the document slots of window.ph
content:
## Two implementations, one hook surface

`GraphQLReactorClient` is a light client for the `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser` hooks. It talks plain GraphQL to a Switchboard and fills the same document slots of `window.ph` that the full in-browser reactor fills, so `useDocument`, `useDispatch` and `useReactorClient` work in a plain web app with **no reactor, no PGLite and no job queue in the bundle**.

Connect and Vetra Studio run the full reactor client; a web app runs this one. Both satisfy `IReactorBrowserClient`, so a component that reads and writes documents moves between them unchanged.

```tsx
import { GraphQLReactorProvider } from "@powerhousedao/reactor-browser/graphql-client";

<GraphQLReactorProvider url="http://localhost:4001/graphql">
  <TodoDemo />
</GraphQLReactorProvider>
```

One provider is the whole integration: it builds the client, publishes it into `window.ph.reactorClient` with a `DocumentCache` over it in `window.ph.documentCache`, and registers the `window.ph` event handlers the hooks read through.

## What it deliberately does not fill

`window.ph.reactorClientModule` always stays empty, so the editor-module hooks find nothing below the provider — `useEditorModules` and `useEditorModuleById` return empty or `undefined`, and `loadFile`, `addDocument`, `addFileWithProgress` and `copyNode` throw or no-op. Render editor components the app imports itself.

`window.ph.vetraPackageManager` is filled **only** when the optional `documentModels` prop is given, via a fixed `StaticPackageManager`, which makes `useDocumentModelModules` and `useDocumentModelModuleById` work. Passing no modules is equally supported: actions are plain data and the Switchboard runs the reducer either way.

> Caveat: the academy Overview page and the Limitations table both state flatly that the provider fills "the document slots and no others" and publishes neither slot. That is stale — the provider's own source and the `GraphQLReactorProvider` prop section describe the `documentModels` path above.

Everything is remote-first: a dispatch is a round trip, and there is no offline queue.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/08-ReactorBrowserClient/01-OverviewAndQuickstart.md and 02-ApiReference.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
